original_question: A II1 factor N is solid if every subalgebra A subset N whose commutant in N is diffuse is amenable, and N is U-solid if every subalgebra A subset N whose commutant in NU is diffuse is amenable. Determine whether solidity and U-solidity are equivalent for II1 factors.
target_in_paper: Problem 44 in the section "Miscellaneous": "Is solidity equivalent to 𝒰-solidity in II_1 factors?" The immediately preceding sentence recalls the definitions of solid and 𝒰-solid. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target very closely. It correctly identifies the two properties being compared, uses the right ambient class (II_1 factors), and encodes the intended amenability criterion through diffuse relative commutants in M and in M^𝒰. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
missing_details: The paper works with a fixed non-principal ultrafilter 𝒰 on ℕ, so a fully stand-alone version should state that 𝒰 is fixed and non-principal, rather than leaving "U" implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
M^𝒰 should be identified explicitly as the tracial ultrapower of the tracial von Neumann algebra M. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
The commutants should be written as relative commutants A' ∩ M and A' ∩ M^𝒰. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
The paper's "subalgebra" here means a von Neumann subalgebra A ⊂ M; saying this explicitly removes ambiguity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

No extra hypotheses such as separability, Connes embeddability, group origin, or strong solidity are part of Problem 44; the scope is simply all II_1 factors. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))

If maximum self-containment is desired, the standard operator-algebra meanings of "diffuse" and "amenable" can be spelled out parenthetically, since the paper treats these as standard and does not restate them locally. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
refined_question: Fix a non-principal ultrafilter 𝒰 on ℕ. For a II_1 factor M, let M^𝒰 denote its tracial ultrapower. Say that M is solid if every von Neumann subalgebra A ⊂ M with diffuse relative commutant A' ∩ M is amenable, and say that M is 𝒰-solid if every von Neumann subalgebra A ⊂ M with diffuse relative commutant A' ∩ M^𝒰 is amenable. Are solidity and 𝒰-solidity equivalent for II_1 factors?
justification: This rewrite stays exactly at the level of the paper's official target. The paper first recalls the two definitions and then asks, as Problem 44, whether they are equivalent for II_1 factors. The opening notation supplies the hidden convention that 𝒰 is a fixed non-principal ultrafilter on ℕ and that M^𝒰 is the tracial ultrapower. The paper also notes there that the question remains open. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2511.20377))
